query: FeNiCrCoCu is considered promising for high-heat wear-resistant use and is suitable for thin-film applications; because bulk preparation is expensive, applying it as a coating on a conventional metal is more practical. Earlier studies reported improved wear or mechanical performance from high-entropy-alloy coatings on Al, Ni, and titanium-alloy substrates, and simulations of FeNiCrCoCu on Cu indicated that sliding speed affects tangential and normal forces. Other work associated composition and grain size with changes in wear damage. However, most prior studies examined a limited operating regime or the properties of the alloys themselves rather than the overall wear resistance of coatings under varied thermal conditions. Subject to retaining FeNiCrCoCu as a coating on a Cu matrix, what single intervention could improve its overall wear resistance during sliding across varied thermal and contact regimes? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its causal mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to an unchanged coating in matched tests, the boundaries within which it should hold, supporting evidence from the introduction, and an experiment with a clear rejection criterion for both the predicted outcome and the proposed mechanism.

generation.hypothesis: Optimizing the grain size of the FeNiCrCoCu coating through controlled annealing can improve its overall wear resistance during sliding across varied thermal and contact regimes.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu coating on a Cu matrix
generation.intervention: Controlled annealing to optimize grain size
generation.mechanism: Reduced wear damage due to improved mechanical properties from optimized grain size
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved wear resistance compared to an unchanged coating in matched tests
generation.boundary: Within the range of thermal and contact regimes typically encountered in high-heat wear-resistant applications
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between grain size and wear resistance may depend on other factors such as composition and substrate material

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the optimized coating shows no significant improvement in wear resistance compared to the unchanged coating, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Gap and lever. Type: limitation. Statement: Increasing the annealing temperature and time to 950 °C for 100 h caused the volume fraction of gamma prime precipitates to decrease in the Hf and Mo alloys, contrary to the base alloy.. System: Al 9.5 Co 25 Cr 8 Fe 15 Ni 36 Ti 6 Hf 0.5 and Al 9 Co 25 Cr 8 Fe 15 Ni 36 Ti 6 Mo 1. Lever: annealing temperature and time. Quote: "While the size of precipitates increased with longer treatment at higher temperatures for the Mo- and Hf-containing alloys, too, the volume fractions of the Heusler type phase and γ′-phase were not enhanced, but decreased about 7–8% in the case of the γ′-phase"

Gap and lever. Type: tradeoff. Statement: Higher rotational speeds (1800 rpm) achieve superior grain refinement and oxidation resistance but result in a bimodal grain distribution and a significant reduction in the fraction of high-angle grain boundaries compared to lower speeds.. System: AlCoCrFeNi High Entropy Alloy. Lever: rotational speed (strain rate). Quote: "The fraction of high angle grain boundaries (HAGBs, θ > 15°) is reduced from nearly 87% for the as-cast sample to ∼82% and 66% for the SFP_400 and SFP_1800 samples, respectively."
